title: How I created an AI game in under 5 minutes using Gemini + free AI game generator (Mobile & Web)
author: Funny-You-2062
selftext:
Wanted to share a quick workflow test on how to create an AI game without writing manual code, using Gemini as the designer and a free builder platform for execution.

**The Workflow:**

1. **Gemini for Design:** I pitched my airship shooter idea to Gemini to outline the visual layout, control scheme, and mechanics.
2. **Execution:** I fed that prompt structure into Klipy (a free AI game generator) to handle the engine, rendering, and logic.
3. **Result:** In under 5 minutes, it compiled a working 3D AI game (*Sky-Pirate Arsenal*).

Attached a video from mobile showing gameplay. It features working altitude sliders, steam pressure meters, radar, and dual port/starboard cannons targeting incoming drone waves. Even though the video is from mobile, it's fully playable in any web browser.

**Observations on AI game development:**

* Having Gemini set strict HUD constraints beforehand made the generator output much cleaner.
* Hitboxes and multi-control UI elements compiled surprisingly well out of the box.
* Juggling altitude sliders and side-cannon buttons on a phone screen takes a minute to get used to.

**Looking for recommendations & tips:**

* **Prompting:** How are you structuring prompts in Gemini to get tighter mechanics for AI game creation?
* **Mobile UI:** Any advice on making multi-button HUD layouts feel smoother on mobile touchscreens?

*(Playable web link in comments)*

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body:
Which is fine, except there's nothing *new* here. There's nothing exciting, interesting, or discussion worthy. You typed a one-shot prompt into a generator to see what it'd spit out without any code. We've all done that and there's dozens of posts here each day that do that. Hell, I have an entire (shitposty) site with my one-shots on it.

*That is not game development*.

If we sound harsh around here, well, we kinda are because we see this stuff every day. People just showing off their one-shot prototypes that anyone is capable of doing.

If you want to have an actual discussion and talk about workflows, how to improve, the best ways and methods to do things, many of us will be glad to help educate you and help you learn. We just don't want to see spammy prototypes with minimal work done. It's fine to be proud of your prototype. But this post basically comes across as "play my prototype!" rather than looking for advice.

**Since you did ask questions**, I will answer them:

>Prompting: How are you structuring prompts in Gemini to get tighter mechanics for AI game creation?

Nobody is seriously using Gemini for game dev (as far as I'm aware). We're using Claude. It's currently the top of the crop when it comes to coding and being able to autonomously build stuff. It struggles graphically (depending on what you're trying to do), but it can't be beat at the moment coding wise.

>Mobile UI: Any advice on making multi-button HUD layouts feel smoother on mobile touchscreens?

Iterate, iterate, iterate. When you're using AI to build stuff, you become a project manager and a QA tester. You have to be able to explain in words specifically what doesn't feel or look right so that it can fix it. You can't say "it doesn't feel responsive enough." You have to say things like "movement with on-screen controls is sluggish as there is a long delay between moving the control left and the player character actually turning to the left. work to reduce the latency between button presses and the resulting movement."

Seriously though, get Claude if you're going to be serious with AI game dev. And also keep in mind that Claude and GPT tend to overtake each other fairly regularly. GPT may be on top in two months, who knows.
